correctness.rationale: Write U=L_{e_0}; U has finite order and L_{e_x}U⁻¹=T_{φx}, so the left envelope is exactly the algebra generated by U and all translations. Over a splitting finite field E the Fourier vectors v_χ diagonalize translations, with projection |G|⁻¹Σ_a χ(a)T_a onto Ev_χ. U takes v_χ to v_{χ∘β⁻¹}, and P_χU^jP_ψ gives an exact matrix unit when the two characters belong to the same β* orbit. Distinct orbit spaces are preserved by every generator. This yields the full split product without any averaging over β or assumption on its order. For a Frobenius cycle of f split blocks, any nonzero descended two-sided ideal must extend to all f blocks by transitivity; the invariant center is E fixed by the f-th Frobenius, hence F_{q^f}. The finite division-ring theorem and dimension f t² give M_t(F_{q^f}). In the natural module the split commutant is one scalar per orbit subspace, and the linear commutation equations descend, proving equality with the center. In C_n there are φ_E(d) characters of order d, all with orbit length ord_d(b), proving both divisor sums with the trivial character included. For C₇, multiplication by 2 has two nontrivial length-three orbits and scalar 3 swaps them; for C₂² the displayed β cycles its three nontrivial characters, giving dimension 10 even in characteristic three. The supplied script was inspected, not run; direct ranks there are checks of dimension, not independent identifications of center fields. The proof covers those fields and the modular hypothesis.

The center fields distinguish which split summands remain separate after descent, and semisimplicity of the realized action in a genuinely modular case answers a question the complex representation does not settle. The arbitrary abelian scope, explicit nonsplit example, and separate commutant description make the result reusable.
